title: Part-time jobs and study
text: Many international students works part-time while they study. A job helps them cover their living costs, and it also gives them chance to practise English with local people. Last year, I work in a café near my university for three month. I was responsible of serving customers and cleaning the kitchen. My manager was kind and let me to choose my own hours, so I could still attend all my classes. After a few weeks, I felt much more confidence when I spoke English. In my experience, a part-time job is useful, but students should not work more than fifteen hours a week.

errors.ruleReminder: A plural subject takes a plural verb: students work, a student works.
errors.explanation: The subject is many international students (plural), so the verb has no -s: work.

errors.ruleReminder: A singular countable noun needs an article (a, an, the) or another determiner.
errors.explanation: Chance is a singular countable noun here, so it needs a or the: gives them a chance.

errors.ruleReminder: Use the past simple for a finished action at a finished time (last year).
errors.explanation: Last year is a finished time, so the verb must be past simple: worked.

errors.ruleReminder: After numbers above one, use a plural noun: two months, three weeks.
errors.explanation: Three is more than one, so the noun must be plural: months.

errors.ruleReminder: Responsible goes with for: responsible for something.
errors.explanation: The fixed phrase is responsible for, not responsible of.

errors.ruleReminder: After let and make, use the base verb with no to: let me choose.
errors.explanation: Let is followed by an object and the base verb, without to.

errors.ruleReminder: After feel and more, use an adjective: feel more confident.
errors.explanation: Confidence is a noun. After felt much more, we need the adjective confident.
